title: Pad See Ew
subtitle: Thai stir-fried wide rice noodles with egg and dark soy sauce
excerpt: Pad see ew is a Thai stir-fried noodle dish with a deeply savoury dark soy sauce coating. Wide rice noodles are tossed with chicken, egg, and Chinese broccoli over very high heat until the noodles have slightly charred edges. It is one of Thailand's most popular street foods.
sourceNotes: Pad see ew means fried with soy sauce. The dish shows clear Chinese influence -- the wide rice noodles (sen yai) are similar to the Chinese ho fun noodles used in Cantonese stir-fries. The dish arrived in Thailand with Chinese immigrants and was adapted with Thai fish sauce and local vegetables.

content.text: The charred edges on the noodles are what make pad see ew worth cooking at home. You need a very hot pan and you need to leave the noodles alone for a full minute to get colour. Resist the urge to toss them constantly -- movement prevents charring.

items.prepNote: use 250g wide rice noodles -- soak in warm water for 20 minutes, then drain
use Chinese broccoli or kale -- cut into 5cm pieces
use dark soy sauce -- for the characteristic colour

content.text: Mix the dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, honey, and salt in a small bowl. This is the sauce.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok or wide frying pan over the highest heat possible. Fry the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken. Stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until just cooked. Remove and set aside.
Add the drained noodles to the hot pan. Spread them in a single layer. Leave for 1 minute without stirring -- this creates the charred edges. Toss, then leave again.
Push the noodles to the side. Add a splash of oil. Crack in the eggs and scramble. Toss with the noodles.
Return the chicken. Add the greens and sauce. Toss everything together over high heat for 1 to 2 minutes. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: Noodles are soft and clumping rather than having charred edges
items.cause: Pan not hot enough or too much food in the pan
items.fix: The pan must be smoking before the noodles go in. Cook in batches if necessary. The noodles need direct contact with the hot surface to char. Moving them too quickly prevents this.

content.text: Pad see ew is a fixture of Thai street food. The deep colour comes from dark soy sauce, which is much thicker and sweeter than regular soy. The slightly charred noodles are the prized element. In Thailand it is sold from street carts alongside pad Thai. It is less well-known internationally but equally good.
